what_its_for: Vonoprazan is used to treat heartburn and acid-related problems. It helps heal and relieve symptoms of erosive esophagitis (damage to your food pipe caused by stomach acid), gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and stomach or small intestine ulcers. It may also be used along with antibiotics to get rid of a stomach infection called H. pylori (Helicobacter pylori).
how_to_take: Take vonoprazan by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you are taking it with antibiotics for an H. pylori infection, make sure to take all medicines exactly as your doctor prescribed and finish the full course, even if you start feeling better.
dosing: The usual dose for heartburn and GERD is 10 mg to 20 mg once daily. For erosive esophagitis, your doctor may start you on 20 mg once daily and then lower the dose to 10 mg once daily for maintenance. For H. pylori infection, you will take a higher dose of 20 mg twice daily along with antibiotics for 14 days. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store vonoprazan at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Store it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking vonoprazan with methotrexate (a medicine used for cancer or arthritis) without talking to your doctor first, as vonoprazan may increase the levels of methotrexate in your body. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because vonoprazan may affect how certain medicines work, including some antifungal medicines like ketoconazole and HIV medicines. Limit alcohol use, as alcohol can worsen stomach acid problems and irritate your stomach lining.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: severe stomach pain; black, tarry, or bloody stools; vomiting blood or something that looks like coffee grounds; chest pain; trouble swallowing; unexplained weight loss; severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling; signs of low magnesium levels such as muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, or seizures; or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Many people start to feel relief from heartburn and acid symptoms within the first few days of starting vonoprazan. However, it may take 1 to 4 weeks to feel the full benefit, especially if you have erosive esophagitis or ulcers. If you do not notice any improvement after 4 weeks, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before taking this medicine, as there is limited information about its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Older adults (65 years and older) can generally take the same dose as younger adults, but should be monitored closely. People with severe liver problems may need a lower dose — be sure to tell your doctor if you have any liver conditions. This medicine is not currently approved for use in children.
